A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPOIL research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-MDP simulations and evaluations on CartPole-v1, Acrobot-v1 and LunarLander-v2 in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds experiments with redundant critic features and linear IQ-Learn comparisons in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same objective, critic best responses, multiplicative policy updates and random-iterate output. The neural approximations are also retained. Revised realizability assumptions do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic linear-MDP imitation and the same three continuous-state benchmarks. The new appendix experiments vary feature representations or comparison methods within the retained linear-MDP task.

E2.justification: v1's linear-MDP comparison evaluates SPOIL against BC. v3 adds IQ-Learn to the simple-expert and neural-expert comparisons in Appendix E.2/Figure 5. The continuous-state comparator set remains IQ-Learn, P2IL and BC.

E3.justification: New Appendix E.1 uses d=3 and adds 20d redundant critic features. E.2 specifies linear critics, matched policy learning rates and selection of the best tested IQ-Learn critic learning rate. Existing benchmark subsampling and best-policy evaluation are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1/Figure 4 adds a targeted test where BC receives compact features while SPOIL receives redundant critic features. This tests the previously discussed condition under which representation complexity can favor BC.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging Figures 1–2 across 10 seeds and retain their uncertainty displays. Added Figure 5 follows the same ten-seed convention; no new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure is specified.

E6.justification: The original Figures 1–2 results are unchanged. Added Figure 4 shows BC learning faster initially, with similar later returns. Figure 5 adds IQ-Learn curves below SPOIL for both expert classes.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–2 now require realizability only for the algorithm's softmax policy classes, whose definitions already appeared in Appendix B.3. v3 normalizes return by 1−γ and corrects Table 1's total-return discount exponents from 2 to 4 for linear approximation and 4 to 8 for general approximation. Proposition 1 also removes the outer expectation from the definition of Δ. The proof appendices otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central arbitrary-expert objective and ε^-2/ε^-4 sample-scaling contributions remain. However, the introductory Table 1 revises SPOIL's total-return discount exponents from 2/4 to 4/8, qualifying the original quantitative comparison.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly explains that realizability of the expert's Q-function is unnecessary. It also removes v1 Appendix F's pessimistic discussion of further relaxations restricted to particular policies, while retaining most other limitations and open questions in Section 6.

D1.justification: The added experiments disclose feature-augmentation dimensions and IQ-Learn learning-rate controls and tuning. Existing neural architectures, Adam settings, PyTorch implementation and code-availability information are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Appendix A are unchanged. v3 adds an explicit contrast with Weisz et al. (2023) and Mhammedi (2024), explaining that SPOIL's revised assumptions concern its softmax policy classes rather than all Markov policies.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. v3 expands the assumptions and normalization explanation, reorganizes Appendix E and incorporates most of Appendix F into Section 6. New Figure 5 references in Sections 5.1 and E.3 incorrectly identify the continuous-state experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 4–5 and repositions Figure 2 while retaining the existing plots and table structure. Figure 5 incorrectly carries a continuous-state-domain caption despite displaying the linear-MDP comparison.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an important theoretical inconsistency: v1 defines unnormalized return, while Lemma 1 and its Appendix B.1 proof use normalized return. Correcting the definition and Table 1's discount dependence substantially improves the interpretation and comparison of the central guarantees. Explicit policy-class assumptions and additional linear comparisons add precision and empirical context. These gains outweigh the limited presentation regression from the misleading Figure 5 caption and cross-references.
